description: The bar chart illustrates the “effect” of morphosyntactic probing across various language families and isolate languages for two multilingual BERT models — mBERT and XLM — under two probing conditions: “targ” (target language probing) and “permute” (cross-lingual probing with permutation). The horizontal axis categorizes languages into nine groups: IE-Baltic, IE-Germanic, IE-Indic, IE-Romance, IE-Slavic, IE-other, Isolate, Semitic, and Uralic. The vertical axis, labeled “effect,” ranges from 0 to 40 with major gridlines at intervals of 10, representing the probing performance metric (likely F1-score or similar). Four bar types are shown per group, color-coded in the legend: light blue for mBERT-targ, dark blue for XLM-targ, light green for mBERT-permute, and dark green for XLM-permute. Error bars (vertical lines with caps) indicate variability or confidence intervals for each bar. In most language families, mBERT-targ and XLM-targ show higher effects than their permute counterparts, with mBERT-targ often leading. Notably, in the “Isolate” category, mBERT-targ reaches the highest effect (~35), while permute effects drop sharply to near zero. The “Uralic” group shows a similar pattern, with mBERT-targ (~29) and XLM-targ (~21) performing well, while permute effects are minimal. In contrast, “IE-Indic” and “IE-Slavic” show relatively balanced performance across conditions, and “IE-Romance” exhibits low permute effects. The bars are not sorted by height, and no bars are visually emphasized beyond color coding and error bars. The chart visually supports the paper’s focus on how multilingual models generalize morphosyntactic knowledge within and across language families.
